scope: Cooperative recover/native-mutex ownership during release, not an adversarial raw filesystem writer.

locations.release: ManagedSource._release_operation unlock/close precede final inode/token checks and unlink
locations.acquisition: ManagedSource._operation recover=True opens the existing lock inode, acquires its OS lock and reuses nonce/token; path identity is not checked until release
locations.mutation: ManagedSource.recover may recreate prune-intent and _finish after opening the previously completed intent

interleaving: A finishes valid recovery and final data sync while holding old inode L.
A unlocks/closes L but has not yet executed the owner-file unlink.
B opens the existing operation.lock inode L and acquires the OS mutex for recover. It reuses the same original nonce/token, so A path/token checks remain true.
A unlinks operation.lock while B owns L.
C creates operation.lock as new inode M for an ordinary operation and acquires M. B and C can now mutate with independent OS locks.
Even if B eventually detects the missing/replaced path during its own release, its recover body can already have recreated intent or changed state.
safetyImpact: No cooperative live-owner guarantee from a nonblocking OS lock once its pathname may be removed by a previous owner after unlock. The exact checked token and inode do not close the check/unlink race.
repairConstraint: Use a stable OS mutex pathname that is never removed, separate from removable owner/failed-operation metadata, or another provably atomic handoff protocol. Do not merely add another path check and claim atomicity.
